0.content:
Khaenri'ah (also: Khaenriah, Kingdom of Khaenri'ah, Dahri): Khaenri'ah was a kingdom of humans deep underground beneath the Sumeru desert. It was the one nation in Teyvat that never had a god. Its people built machines, worked alchemy that could create life, and dreamed of standing above the gods' order; Dainsleif calls it "the pride of humankind." Five hundred years ago its rulers' use of Abyssal power set off the cataclysm, and the Heavenly Principles and the gods destroyed it. Its survivors were cursed: pure-blooded Khaenri'ahns cannot die, and those of mixed blood became monsters. In Sumeru it is also called Dahri.

Two royal lines ruled it: first the Crimson Moon Dynasty, then the Eclipse Dynasty, whose last Vinster King was Irmin. Pure-blooded Khaenri'ahns are marked by four-pointed star pupils. Ruin Machines, the Abyss Order and the hilichurls all come from Khaenri'ah, and so do Dainsleif, Kaeya's family and the Fatui Director Pierro. In 7.1 it was revealed that all Khaenri'ahns descend from the Tsaritsa Anastasya and the Third Descender Saarelainen, which is why they honour her as the "Mother of Khaenri'ah".

Geography: A subterranean realm beneath the Sumeru desert, dark and almost barren of natural life. Kaeya says only that it was "deep underground somewhere near Sumeru". A great sealed gate in Gavireh Lajavard, in the Girdle of the Sands, is said to lead down to the ruined kingdom.

Its founders once lived on the surface, and in old legend few later Khaenri'ahns had ever seen the sun or the sea. The mage Barbeloth says Khaenri'ah had several large underground lakes. Water there could reflect the sea of stars beyond the false sky, and space in that region was unusually unstable. The legend Perinheri adds that the kingdom's position let things from outside the world leak in, and its army wiped out the dangerous ones. The legend also mentions a "Sea of Wells". When the gods struck during the cataclysm, the skies turned red and filled with crimson cubes, and the land the kingdom stood on was torn apart and flooded with lava.

Places: Named institutions and places: the royal palace with its dungeons, where the Court of Khaenri'ah sat; the Universitas Magistrorum, the royal research academy; the Royal Library, whose banned texts were closed even to nobles; and the Royal Machine Workshop "Gnade", whose smelting furnace was abandoned before the fall. On the surface, Khaenri'ahn ruins reached through Gavireh Lajavard include an Azosite-powered machine workshop and proving ground, the last in the kingdom to use that power system. The Ruins of Dahri in Sumeru and the Schwanenritter's giant Ruin Golems date from the exodus. Dainsleif says the Inverted City in the Chasm's underground mines looks somewhat like Khaenri'ahn ruins and had ties to its civilisation.

People: Khaenri'ahns descend from Anastasya and Saarelainen. Pure-bloods count as a people distinct from the surface nations: their pupils are four-pointed stars, while descendants of the Crimson Moon Dynasty have red X-shaped pupils. A heavily diluted bloodline may show no mark at all. Outsiders from the surface also came to live in Khaenri'ah; in the legend Perinheri, a princess who would not submit to Morax drifts in through its gates. Khaenri'ahns whose ancestry lay in the gods' lands were later cursed differently from pure-bloods.

Society was a stratified monarchy with a proud, "obstinately pure-blooded" aristocracy. Known Khaenri'ahns: Dainsleif, captain of the royal guard; his brother Vedrfolnir "The Visionary", the court's seer; Hroptatyr "The Wise", president of the Universitas, with Eftirvit (now Pierro) as vice-president; the alchemist Rhinedottir "Gold"; Surtalogi "The Foul"; Rerir, an agent of the intelligence service; the knight-commander Thrain (now Il Capitano); the knights Halfdan and Haden; the Alberichs Anfortas and Chlothar; the Moon Marrow researcher Tholindis; the exiled monk Rauthvangi (Rotwang); and Direidyth, a village girl. Albedo was made by Rhinedottir long after the fall and says he has no attachment to Khaenri'ah. Arlecchino is of Crimson Moon blood. Kaeya is of the Alberich Clan.

Government: Khaenri'ah was a hereditary monarchy. In the Eclipse era the "Vinster King" ruled with the Court of Khaenri'ah. Under him were royal mages (Hroptatyr was Chief Royal Mage), the Universitas Magistrorum, several knightly orders, and an intelligence service. Irmin was the last king, and his closest advisers were Hroptatyr and Vedrfolnir.

In the final crisis a bulletin announced that, with Irmin "indisposed" and unknown threats facing the kingdom, Knight Marshal Anfortas would serve as temporary Regent and lead the Regnum Concilium Ultimum until order returned. The Alberich Clan, which had no royal blood, later taught its children that it stepped in as regent when the one-eyed king's strength failed. In the earlier Crimson Moon era, the legend Perinheri shows a ruler who let a sage found an orphanage for children who had come from beyond the world.

Religion: No god ever ruled Khaenri'ah. It was not abandoned by one; it never had one. Its people suspected that the Heavenly Principles were outsiders who had usurped the world, knew the rumour that Teyvat's sky is false, and planned to rise above "the fundamental principles" of the world. The motto behind the war machines was that land is not tilled with farm tools but won "with steel and blood."

Early in the Crimson Moon Dynasty, priests convinced a "muddle-minded king" that the Crimson Moon was all-powerful and spread its worship. The Crimson Moon was the Iridescent Moon's remains fused with the Abyss. The priests likely wanted it as a link to the Abyss. Khaenri'ahn astrologers later glimpsed the origin of all fate in the false sky's inverted image, which helped bring that dynasty down. Hilichurls of the Eclipse Tribe still draw eclipse symbols whose meaning only their shaman knows.

Economy: Little grew underground. People ate mostly meat and mushrooms, including alchemically engineered strains, and imported grain. In Irmin's last years grain imports were falling. Buildings were mostly of stone. Energy came from Azosite, refined from pure elemental energy of the ley lines and pressed into energy blocks in large smelting works. Industry ran on machine workshops and the mass production of Ruin Machines.

Technology: Khaenri'ah built the war automatons now called Ruin Machines. The Ruin Guard's original name was "Field Tiller". The machines can repair themselves and keep working for centuries. After the fall they wandered Teyvat without a purpose and gathered at ruins. Its alchemy, the Art of Khemia, could create life, which mattered in a land with little natural life.

Khaenri'ahns were "obsessed with mimesis": copying and improving on natural forms, even dragons and Hypostases. Under Irmin the kingdom spied on "secrets from beyond the skies" so that its machines could "throw off the shackles" of the world's laws. One engineer begged the Knight Marshal to save machines built to the old standard, trusting human will over gods and demons alike. The Universitas Magistrorum studied astrology, alchemy, Moon Marrow and the Abyss. It predicted for the king that two stars, apparently the twins, would be caught by Teyvat's gravity. Eftirvit and Hroptatyr theorised about one day summoning "the essence of Celestia itself".

Foreign relations: Khaenri'ah's godlessness was known all over Teyvat, and people from the Seven Nations went there to live. More than 2,000 years ago its diplomats, among them Oogura and Ooshima, came to Enkanomiya looking for proof that the gods were usurpers. They tried to steal the forbidden book Before Sun and Moon, and Antei destroyed their Ruin Guard at the cost of his life. Ruin Machines were already on the surface during the Archon War, when Guizhong collected some. After the fall, survivors were widely distrusted. In Sumeru, however, the sage Nagarjuna fought beside the Schwanenritter and called them "heroes of Dahri", and in Natlan the chief Ayizu befriended the refugee Thrain.

History: Khaenri'ah was founded as a godless nation around the time Sal Vindagnyr fell, thousands of years ago. The Crimson Moon Dynasty ruled first and was overthrown by the Eclipse Dynasty. Five hundred years ago King Irmin named the newly arrived Traveler's sibling his heir and "Savior", then used them as a vessel to absorb unlimited Abyssal power. When he blinded Vedrfolnir for warning him, Dainsleif and four others stormed the palace. All five turned on Dainsleif and took the Abyssal power, becoming the Five Sinners. Abyssal monsters poured across Teyvat, Celestia and the gods destroyed the kingdom, and Ronova cursed its people.

Under Irmin the Universitas was turned over to Abyssal research. Rerir served as a secret executioner of Crimson Moon descendants, and Irmin grew more obsessed and erratic. During the palace coup the king set off "secret mechanisms" that seemingly drew Abyssal monsters to the palace. Each Sinner took one sixth of the power the sibling had absorbed, and none of them defended Khaenri'ah. Rhinedottir's creatures, among them the dragon Durin and the Riftwolves, ravaged the nations. During the cataclysm the Electro Archon Makoto died in Khaenri'ah, and the Hydro Archon Egeria fell holding back the corruption at Tunigi Hollow. The sibling, told by Direidyth that the Traveler was looking for them, left the dying kingdom to wake their twin. Asmoday caught and separated the twins as they tried to leave Teyvat.

Atmosphere: Picture a kingdom of stone halls under a rock sky, lit by machine light and alchemy instead of the sun. Its people were proud, learned and armed, and lived among brass-lined machines, laboratories and academies. They prized human will and resented the gods, and the nobility was strictly conscious of rank and blood. In its last years it was a frightened, suspicious court where speaking against the king could cost you your eyes. The surviving ruins are vast in scale and feel industrial.

Dangers: Today: Ruin Machines that still guard old sites; cursed remnants such as Shadowy Husks; Abyss Order mages, heralds and lectors; Riftwolves; and lingering Abyssal corruption. Forbidden knowledge and Abyssal energy corrupt land, ley lines and minds.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Khaenri'ah lies in ruins and its gate is sealed. It has not been visited in the main story. Its survivors are scattered and cursed, the Abyss Order fights to revive it, and its final Archon Quest chapter is announced but not released.

The Heavenly Principles have been asleep since the cataclysm. In 7.1 Anastasya concluded that destroying Khaenri'ah triggered the Third Descender's curse, which had been meant to protect his descendants. The Abyss Order, led by the Traveler's sibling, holds the woven ley lines of a "New Khaenri'ah" and is looking for somewhere to lay them down.

1.content:
The Crimson Moon Dynasty was Khaenri'ah's first known royal line. It ruled when "a crimson moon shone" over the underground realm. Its priests had the people worship the Crimson Moon, the Abyss-fused remains of the Iridescent Moon, and its royal blood carries the Abyssal "Balemoon Bloodfire". The dynasty sealed the Crimson Moon and its corrupted Moon Marrow inside a domain that only the Bloodfire can open. Alchemy and the warbeasts of the Beastmaster Knights flourished. A coup put the Eclipse Dynasty on the throne. Arlecchino suggests the usurpers opposed a direct link to the Abyss, or that an ideological split drove them. Irmin later ordered its descendants exterminated, yet the line survives in Arlecchino.

Bloodfire users risk Abyssal corruption reaching the heart, which turns the user into someone else entirely. Descendants carried on secretly. In All Is Foretold, the survivor Orlog dreamed of restoring the dynasty, and Tholindis of a distant branch family hid her blood even from her fiancé Rerir.

2.comment: Khaenri'ah: Eclipse Dynasty and King Irmin
2.content:
The Eclipse Dynasty (literally "Black Sun") replaced the Crimson Moon Dynasty and ruled until the cataclysm. It favoured mechanical engineering and, at the end, "secrets from beyond the skies." Its last Vinster King, the one-eyed Irmin, trusted Hroptatyr and Vedrfolnir above all. He made the Traveler's sibling his heir, used them to absorb Abyssal power, turned the Universitas over to Abyssal research, and blinded Vedrfolnir for prophesying ruin. His fate after the palace coup is unclear.

Rhinedottir mocked how qualifications did not decide who rose in Khaenri'ah. Hroptatyr admitted he only received a senior post so young because the king was "such an extremist". Pierro says he tried and failed to turn Irmin away from Abyssal power.

3.comment: Khaenri'ah: The Five Sinners of Khaenri'ah
3.content:
The Five Sinners were among Khaenri'ah's most esteemed people: Rhinedottir "Gold" (Life), Vedrfolnir "The Visionary" (Time), Surtalogi "The Foul" (Void), Hroptatyr "The Wise" (Reason) and Rerir "Rächer of Solnari" (Death). Dainsleif gathered them to rescue his brother. Instead, each took one sixth of the world-shattering Abyssal power Irmin had poured into the Traveler's sibling. None defended Khaenri'ah as it fell. Hroptatyr was one of the "four pillars" of the kingdom.

Afterwards they went their separate ways. Rhinedottir created Albedo and later devoured Naberius' heart to become Ruler of Life. Hroptatyr gave his memories to Eftirvit and left to merge with the Abyss in the sea of stars. Vedrfolnir was found as a chained crystal in Sumeru's Avidya Forest and empowered Chlothar. Surtalogi trained Skirk. Rerir led the Wild Hunt in Nod-Krai until he was driven out.

4.content: The Universitas Magistrorum was the kingdom's royal academy, directly under the king. It worked in astrology, alchemy and other arts, and also trained fighters. In the last years Hroptatyr was its president and Eftirvit (Pierro) its vice-president. Both had studied under Professor Mimameith, who fell fatally ill after working on the king's Abyssal research. When Irmin became obsessed with the Abyss, all staff were moved to Abyssal research except the Moon Marrow researcher Tholindis.

5.comment: Khaenri'ah: The Schwanenritter and the Exodus to Sumeru
5.content:
As dark beasts overran the kingdom, Knight Marshal Anfortas declared himself Regent. His Schwanenritter ("Swan Knights") led able-bodied survivors to the surface through the Girdle of the Sands into Sumeru, fighting with Ruin Golems they called "Mechanical Wardens". On the surface many refugees fell ill and turned into monsters. The knights fought on in Dharma Forest beside the sage Nagarjuna, who named them "heroes of Dahri". Ynghildr vanished in battle and Hildric died of illness. Anfortas killed the traitor Hadura, losing his left eye, gave him a knight's funeral anyway, and fought alone until his presumed death.

Hadura had earned the title "Sentinel of the Golden Hall" for stalling the beasts. Ynghildr survived as a Shadowy Husk guarding a fallen golem until the Traveler defeated her. Nagarjuna's followers carried the knights' will into the desert as the Order of Skeptics.

6.content: The Alberich Clan was a noble Khaenri'ahn house known for producing leaders of the knights. It acted as regent when Irmin failed, a history Kaeya was taught in childhood; his secret notes on it were found during the limited-time event Hidden Strife. During the cataclysm Chlothar Alberich, a pure-blood, was cursed with immortality, and his son Caribert, whose mother came from Mondstadt, became a hilichurl. Chlothar later founded the Abyss Order. About ten years ago Kaeya's father left him near the Dawn Winery as an agent of Khaenri'ah, calling him "our last hope". Kaeya has since turned away from that mission.

7.comment: Khaenri'ah: The Royal Guard and the Black Serpents
7.content: The Black Serpent Knights were the royal guard, with Dainsleif, the "Twilight Sword", as captain. During the cataclysm Dainsleif ordered his knight Halfdan to protect the people at all costs. The curse turned the guard into Shadowy Husks and eroded knights who have lost most of their memories. In the Chasm, Halfdan's band still guarded hilichurls as Khaenri'ahn citizens, until Dainsleif released him. Dainsleif could make out only one word of their speech in the old tongue: "run".

8.content: After the Traveler's sibling arrived, Irmin and the court proclaimed them heir to the throne and a prophesied "Savior" who would bring the kingdom a bright future. A young Dainsleif attended the ceremony. Ordinary people hoped too: Direidyth's grandmother told her stories of a Savior who would rescue Khaenri'ahns at doomsday. Through a time overlap Istaroth arranged in present-day Natlan, Direidyth met the Traveler. When she later told the sibling about it, the sibling left Khaenri'ah to find their twin.

9.content: In 7.1 Rhinedottir told the Tsaritsa that every Khaenri'ahn descends from her and the Third Descender, Saarelainen. (The trailer "Sudden Snow" shows that their son had four-pointed star pupils.) To restore Anastasya after the Heavenly Principles erased her, Saarelainen gave his body to become the seven Gnoses. In return he secured a promise that his descendants would never be harmed, backed by a curse that would strike if the promise broke. Anastasya concluded that the cataclysm triggered it, putting the Heavenly Principles to sleep. She knew of the bloodline but had no memory of it. Khaenri'ahns honour her as "Mother of Khaenri'ah", and Dainsleif came to an audience with her for that reason.

10.comment: Khaenri'ah: The Curses on the Khaenri'ahns
10.content:
After the cataclysm Ronova, the Shade of Death, cursed every Khaenri'ahn. Pure-bloods were judged "the greater sinners" and given immortality: they cannot die or age, but they still suffer erosion, which wears down body and mind. Most became Abyss Mages, Heralds and Lectors. Those descended from people of the gods' lands received the "curse of the wilderness" and turned into hilichurls.

The royal guard became Shadowy Husks or eroded Black Serpent Knights. Dainsleif kept his mind and form thanks to a ring from Vedrfolnir that keeps resetting his body. Capitano told Ronova that most of the people she cursed knew nothing of the Five Sinners' crimes. Before the fall, Hroptatyr had found a way to draw the Authority of Death from the Crimson Moon to make people undying, and he came to see that "blessing" as a curse. Dainsleif hopes that cleansed hilichurls could one day be the foundation of a rebuilt Khaenri'ah.

11.content: In 7.1 the Fatui unsealed Hroptatyr's notebook in Snezhnaya. It was nearly blank, because purging forbidden knowledge from Irminsul had erased most of it, but a prism hidden inside it held an interactive memory of him as a young scholar at the Universitas with Eftirvit and their teacher Mimameith. In it he spoke of a parable he had heard from an "extraordinary acquaintance", whom Pierro identifies as Vedrfolnir: two blond crowned heirs seek the Genesis Pearl, and the first "will answer my call". Pierro then revealed that when he summoned Paimon from Celestia, Hroptatyr summoned the Traveler's sibling at the same time. Dainsleif found this young Hroptatyr disappointing, since he had not yet seen Khaenri'ah's dark side.

12.content: The Abyss Order wants to revive Khaenri'ah and take revenge on The Seven and Celestia. With the Loom of Fate, the Traveler's sibling wove ley lines for a new Khaenri'ah inside Natlan's Night Kingdom, building on an Inteyvat flower and on memories of the kingdom from Order members and Dainsleif. The result, the Atlas of the New World, holds those ley lines and still needs a place to be laid down. The sibling means to face the Heavenly Principles "as equals" with a whole world behind them.

13.content: The Inteyvat is Khaenri'ah's national flower, five petals in white and pale blue, and it once bloomed all over the kingdom. Dainsleif says it wilts after two weeks. Plucked and carried out of Khaenri'ah, its petals turn hard, and they only soften and crumble to dust once returned home, so it stands for a wanderer far from home. Lumine wears one in her hair.
